nodes.name: HM Revenue and Customs
nodes.summary: The UK tax authority responsible for administering and collecting taxes.

nodes.name: UK tax system
nodes.summary: The overall structure of UK taxes, including direct and indirect taxes and their legal sources.

nodes.name: Direct taxes
nodes.summary: Taxes imposed directly on income, profits, or gains of taxpayers.

nodes.name: Indirect taxes
nodes.summary: Taxes charged through transactions or consumption rather than directly on a taxpayer's income or gains.

nodes.name: Income tax
nodes.summary: A direct tax computed by applying the income-tax framework to taxable income after relevant allowances and reliefs.

nodes.name: Taxable income
nodes.summary: Income falling within the income-tax charge after classification and permitted deductions, allowances, or reliefs.

nodes.name: Tax assessment
nodes.summary: The process of establishing or correcting the amount of tax for which a taxpayer is liable.

nodes.name: Property income
nodes.summary: Income arising from property interests and property businesses, subject to classification and allowable-expense rules.

nodes.name: Employment income
nodes.summary: Remuneration and taxable benefits arising from employment, considered alongside employment-related expenses.

nodes.name: Pension income
nodes.summary: Income from pensions and the related treatment of pension contributions in individual income-tax computations.

nodes.name: Trading income
nodes.summary: Income from self-employment or a trade, computed by adjusting accounting profit to arrive at taxable profit.

nodes.name: Partnership profits and losses
nodes.summary: Partnership results allocated among partners and brought into each partner's individual tax computation.

nodes.name: National Insurance contributions
nodes.summary: Contributions whose categories and liabilities interact with employment and self-employment income.

nodes.name: Individual tax liability
nodes.summary: The combined tax outcome after bringing together an individual's income sources, allowances, rates, reliefs, and payment obligations.

nodes.name: The UK tax system distinguishes direct and indirect taxes
nodes.summary: The tax-system foundation organizes taxes by whether they are imposed directly on income, profits, or gains or arise through transactions and consumption.

nodes.name: Income-tax liability is derived from taxable income
nodes.summary: The income-tax framework moves from identifying taxable income to applying allowances, rates, and reliefs to determine liability.

nodes.name: Assessment establishes or corrects a taxpayer's liability
nodes.summary: Assessment is the administrative mechanism for establishing or correcting the liability produced by the substantive tax computation.

nodes.name: Multiple income sources feed an individual's total liability
nodes.summary: Property, employment, pension, and trading income are distinct categories that can be brought together in an individual's overall income-tax computation.

nodes.name: Self-employment taxable profit is derived from accounting profit
nodes.summary: Self-employment computation requires adjustments from accounting profit to the profit recognized for tax purposes.

nodes.name: Partnership results are allocated to individual partners
nodes.summary: Partnership profits and losses are allocated among partners and then included in the partners' individual tax computations.

nodes.name: National Insurance interacts with employment and self-employment income
nodes.summary: National Insurance categories and liabilities are connected to the taxpayer's employment and self-employment status and income.

nodes.name: Employment computation distinguishes remuneration from allowable expenses
nodes.summary: Employment income analysis separates taxable remuneration and benefits from expenses that may be allowable for tax purposes.

nodes.name: Tax administration operationalizes substantive liability
nodes.summary: Registration, returns, payment, assessment, records, enquiries, penalties, and appeals provide the administrative lifecycle for tax liabilities.

nodes.name: Self-employment income
nodes.summary: Trading income of self-employed individuals is a context in which National Insurance liability is considered.

nodes.name: Individual tax administration
nodes.summary: Administrative lifecycle covering registration, returns, deadlines, payment, records, enquiries, penalties, and appeals for individuals.

nodes.name: Corporation-tax computation
nodes.summary: Computation of a company’s taxable total profits, rates, reliefs, and payment considerations.

nodes.name: Company loss relief
nodes.summary: Relief mechanisms for company losses against profits across periods or in a corporate group context.

nodes.name: Corporate group
nodes.summary: A group relationship used to analyze loss relief, asset transfers, and planning constraints between companies.

nodes.name: Corporate tax administration
nodes.summary: Company filing, payment, compliance, enquiry, and penalty processes.

nodes.name: Capital-gains framework
nodes.summary: General structure for disposals, gains and losses, allowable costs, annual exemptions, rates, and computations.

nodes.name: Special capital-gains treatment
nodes.summary: Rules for transactions or assets requiring treatment different from the standard capital-gains disposal computation.

nodes.name: NIC connects income categories to individual liability computations
nodes.summary: National Insurance is analyzed in relation to employment and self-employment income and to the wider calculation of individual tax liabilities.

nodes.name: Individual tax administration is a process chain
nodes.summary: The individual administration article groups registration, filing, deadlines, payment, record keeping, enquiries, penalties, and appeals into one compliance lifecycle.

nodes.name: Corporation tax is the corporate computation hub
nodes.summary: The corporation-tax computation provides the central connection between taxable profits, company losses, groups, corporate administration, corporate gains, and VAT context.

nodes.name: Company losses can operate across periods and group context
nodes.summary: Company loss rules address relief against profits across periods and also interact with the corporate-group context.

nodes.name: Group taxation links relief, asset transfers, and planning constraints
nodes.summary: The group-taxation topic combines group relationships with loss relief, asset transfers, and constraints on planning.

nodes.name: Corporate administration operationalizes corporation tax
nodes.summary: Company filing, payment, compliance, enquiry, and penalty rules provide the administrative counterpart to corporation-tax computation.

nodes.name: The standard CGT framework precedes special cases
nodes.summary: The general capital-gains framework supplies the baseline for handling special transactions or assets that require different treatment.

nodes.name: Special CGT cases interact with shares and reliefs
nodes.summary: Special capital-gains cases are positioned alongside share disposals and reorganisations and capital-gains reliefs rather than as an isolated computation.

edges.claim: Share transactions may require relief analysis in addition to the ordinary gains computation.
Relief conditions can be relevant when gains arise to companies.
Inheritance-tax revision intersects with relief concepts and transfer analysis.
Special and overseas VAT issues extend the VAT fundamentals.
Place-of-supply rules illustrate the distinction between direct and indirect tax treatment.
The staged study workflow culminates in integrated exam practice.
VAT questions exemplify the need to classify the taxpayer, transaction, liability, and compliance rules.
Share-disposal questions require classification, computation, relief selection, and administrative checks.
Inheritance-tax questions fit the same classify, compute, relieve, and check workflow.
